patterns.usage_note: Lifts something out as what the sentence is about, which is why it presents known or already-established information while が introduces what is new. が and を are replaced by は outright; へ, で, から, まで and と are kept in front of it (へは, までは, からは), and に is normally kept too, though it is often dropped with time expressions (三時は無理だ). In that stacked position it usually adds contrast: 大阪へは行った implies somewhere else was skipped. It also attaches to the て-form (ては), where the sense is conditional rather than contrastive.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]は毎朝[まいあさ]、犬[いぬ]と公園[こうえん]を走[はし]っています。
examples.english: As for me, I run in the park with my dog every morning.

examples.ruby: 大阪[おおさか]へは行[い]きましたが、神戸[こうべ]へは寄[よ]りませんでした。
examples.english: I did go to Osaka, but I didn't stop by Kobe.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]の昼[ひる]までは家[いえ]で仕事[しごと]をしています。
examples.english: Up until noon tomorrow, at least, I'll be working from home.
